change.description: Separate Console Memo detail navigation from the dedicated author preview, load the current Memo projection server-side with the existing identity and media boundaries, preserve same-route editing and public route history, hide unauthorized private Memo and clipping reads behind the existing missing-resource boundary, and ship a complete official Web Demo covering admin, guest, private, draft, public, clipping, preview, history, and Inspector mutation states.
change.release_unit_description: static frontend and full-feature Docker image

planned.reasoning: The change preserves public API payload shapes, database and local-content formats, public snapshot generation, and deployment host resolution. It adds compatible Console navigation and server-rendered administrator detail projection while making unauthorized private reads indistinguishable from missing resources.

current.reasoning: The candidate changes only the Console Memo detail/preview boundary, request-scoped initial projection, unauthorized read status mapping, shared route history state, and the official build-time Web Demo evidence surface. Public API payload shapes, persistent state, snapshot publishing, and deployment host configuration remain unchanged; the deliberate 403-to-404 mapping for unauthorized private reads makes them indistinguishable from missing resources, while the Demo uses an explicit guest projection that omits authoring-only fields. Console guests now use the current request-scoped public API projection and cannot fall back to a lagging public snapshot after a Memo becomes private or draft. The current candidate also keeps administrator tools inside the Memo detail reading surface on desktop and mobile.

scope_drift.description: The candidate remains within the locked Memo detail/preview, SSR authorization, media/clipping projection, and shared history scope; no schema, public payload, snapshot, host configuration, or VERSION change was introduced.

verified.reasoning: Focused component, Console projection, page-data source selection, clipping, HTTP compatibility, official Web Demo build, and Console browser acceptance checks pass at desktop and mobile viewports. The implementation preserves existing public payload shapes and persistent state while enforcing the same-origin detail/preview boundary and private-resource non-disclosure; the 403-to-404 status change is an intentional compatible privacy hardening because private and missing resources share the documented not-found response. Console runtime now refuses snapshot fallback when the current request has no authorized Memo projection. The focused Web Demo evidence additionally asserts that the administrator toolbar is contained by the visible detail card and that the mobile Inspector control does not occlude the discussion action.
